html:
The Lamian War of 323 to 322 BCE was a revolt by Athens and a large group of Greek states against the rule of Macedon, launched as soon as news came that Alexander the Great had died.

Anger had been building. In 324 BCE Alexander ordered the Greek cities to take back all their exiles, which threatened Athens' hold on the island of Samos. When he died, the Athenian general Leosthenes, with the Aetolians and many others, marched north and trapped the Macedonian regent Antipater in the town of Lamia, which gave the war its name.

The Greeks did well at first, but Leosthenes was killed. Macedonian reinforcements arrived from Asia. In 322 BCE the Athenian fleet was beaten at Amorgos, the last time Athens fought as a real sea power, and the Greek army lost at Crannon.

The terms were hard. Antipater put a garrison in Piraeus and limited Athenian citizenship to men with property, ending Athenian democracy as it had been. The leaders of the revolt were hunted down, and Demosthenes took poison rather than be caught. It was the last time Athens acted as an independent power.
sum: The Lamian War of 323 to 322 BCE was a revolt by Athens and a large group of Greek states against the rule of Macedon, launched as soon as news came that Alexander the Great had died.
